finding.claim: An unauthenticated token with an unknown or missing kid forces an outbound JWKS fetch on every request, bypassing the cache and with no negative caching or rate limit.
finding.source: kid from the unverified token header, read at jwks_client.py:239-241 via decode with verify_signature False

trace.note: Unverified decode of the token; kid is taken from the attacker-supplied header
get_signing_key(header.get('kid')) with attacker-chosen kid
Lookup in cached JWK set; misses for unknown kid
Refresh path calls get_signing_keys(refresh=True), which skips the cache
fetch_data() invoked because refresh bypasses cache
Outbound HTTP request to the configured JWKS URI

finding.guards_checked: kid is only compared with == in match_kid (jwks_client.py:257), never used in a path, URL or query; signing keys filtered to sig/unspecified with a kid (:189-193); JWKS URI is app-configured with http/https only (:90-95); no rate limit or negative cache exists; precondition is use of get_signing_key_from_jwt or get_signing_key with attacker-controlled kid

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, signing keys cached by kid never expire on time, so a key removed from the JWKS after compromise or revocation keeps verifying tokens until LRU eviction.
finding.source: A token whose kid matches a previously cached key, after the key was revoked or removed from the JWKS
finding.sink: Signature verification succeeds with the cached PyJWK

trace.note: get_signing_key wrapped in lru_cache keyed on kid
Enabled only when cache_keys=True
TTL applies only to Tier-1 JWK set cache, not to the per-kid LRU cache

finding.guards_checked: Documented in PyJWKClient docstring (jwks_client.py:57-60); cache_keys defaults to False; eviction only when size exceeds max_cached_keys (default 16)
finding.repro: Create PyJWKClient(uri, cache_keys=True); verify a token with kid K; remove K from the JWKS; verify another token signed by K after the 5-minute JWK set TTL: it still succeeds until 16 other kids evict it.

finding.claim: Issuer validation is silently skipped when no issuer argument is passed, even though verify_iss defaults to True, unlike audience validation which rejects tokens carrying aud when no audience is given.
finding.source: iss claim of a token signed by the verification key

trace.note: verify_iss defaults True so _validate_iss is called
_validate_iss invoked with issuer argument, which is None when app omits it
if issuer is None: return, so iss is not checked
Contrast: _validate_aud rejects a token with aud when audience is None (lines 522-527)

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification is still required before claims are checked; impact depends on the app sharing one verification key or JWKS across multiple issuers or tenants and omitting issuer=; logic inconsistency rather than a direct bypass

finding.claim: Non-numeric iat, nbf or exp values (list, dict, or JSON Infinity) raise TypeError or OverflowError instead of a PyJWT error, because only ValueError is caught.
finding.source: iat, nbf or exp claim of a signed token, or of an unverified token decoded with verify_signature False and explicit verify_* True
finding.sink: int(payload[...]) in claim validation raises an uncaught non-PyJWT exception out of decode()

trace.note: int(payload['iat']) with list value raises TypeError
except ValueError does not catch TypeError or OverflowError
Same pattern for nbf (catches only ValueError)
Same pattern for exp (catches only ValueError)

finding.guards_checked: Default verify_signature False path disables these checks via _merge_options (api_jwt.py:82-89); signed tokens require a valid signature first; impact is an unhandled exception (typically 500) rather than acceptance of a forged token, unless the app treats non-InvalidTokenError exceptions as success

finding.claim: Short HMAC secrets and RSA keys below 2048 bits only produce a warning by default, so weak key material is accepted and can be brute-forced offline from observed tokens.
finding.source: Developer-supplied secret or key (not attacker-controlled); attacker holds an observed HS256 token
finding.sink: HMAC signing and verification with a short secret, enabling offline brute force of the key

trace.note: enforce_minimum_key_length defaults to False
Key length check only raises when enforce_minimum_key_length is True
Otherwise emits InsecureKeyLengthWarning and proceeds
HMAC check_key_length returns message for keys shorter than hash digest size
RSA check_key_length returns message for keys under 2048 bits

finding.guards_checked: Documented design choice with a warning; enforcement is opt-in; precondition is that the application uses a short secret or small RSA key
